biological.citation: Cardiac ryanodine receptor calcium release deficiency syndrome (PMID: 33536282)
biological.summary: RYR2 loss-of-function mutations cause a novel disease entity (CRDS) characterized by sudden cardiac death with normal exercise stress testing. RYR2 LOF mutations result in deficient calcium release from the sarcoplasmic reticulum, leading to cardiac electrophysiological remodeling and increased propensity for early afterdepolarizations. LBLPS pacing protocol reliably induces ventricular arrhythmias in RYR2 LOF mutation carriers.
biological.sample_size: 6 families with RYR2 LOF mutations plus mouse model

biological.citation: RYR2-ryanodinopathies: from calcium overload to calcium deficiency (PMID: 37387319)
biological.summary: RYR2 is the cardiac sarcoplasmic reticulum calcium release channel essential for excitation-contraction coupling and intracellular calcium homeostasis. RYR2 gain-of-function mutations cause CPVT through excessive spontaneous SR calcium release, while loss-of-function variants cause calcium release deficiency syndrome (CRDS). RYR2 mutations represent distinct cardiac ryanodinopathies with different pathophysiological mechanisms.

biological.citation: Heart failure-induced cognitive dysfunction is mediated by intracellular Ca(2+) leak through ryanodine receptor type 2 (PMID: 37429912)
biological.summary: RYR2 undergoes post-translational modifications (PKA phosphorylation, oxidation, nitrosylation, calstabin2 depletion) in hippocampal neurons from heart failure patients and mice, resulting in pathological calcium leak. RYR2 stabilizer drug S107, beta blockers, and TGF-β inhibitors protect against HF-induced cognitive dysfunction by preventing RYR2 calcium leak.
biological.sample_size: Hippocampal neurons from HF patients and mice; HF mouse models

biological.citation: Hippo-Yap Signaling Maintains Sinoatrial Node Homeostasis (PMID: 36317529)
biological.summary: RYR2 is a direct transcriptional target of Yap in sinoatrial node pacemaker cells. Lats1/2 inactivation causes dysregulated calcium handling and decreased Ryr2 expression in the SAN. Yap regulates genes critical for calcium homeostasis including Ryr2, linking the Hippo-Yap pathway to RYR2-mediated calcium regulation in cardiac pacemaker function.

biological.citation: Increased Ca(2+) Transient Underlies RyR2-Related Left Ventricular Noncompaction (PMID: 37325910)
biological.summary: RYR2-I4855M loss-of-function mutation increases peak calcium transient by increasing calcium-induced calcium release gain and elevates end-diastolic calcium by prolonging calcium transient decay. The mutation abolishes store-overload-induced calcium release, elevates SR calcium load, and increases phosphorylated CaMKII levels, underlying RYR2-associated left ventricular noncompaction.

biological.citation: Ero1α-Dependent ERp44 Dissociation From RyR2 Contributes to Cardiac Arrhythmia (PMID: 35086342)
biological.summary: RYR2 forms a redox-sensitive intraluminal complex with ERp44 mediated by cysteine 4806. Ero1α-mediated oxidation causes ERp44 dissociation from RYR2, increasing channel activity and spontaneous calcium release. Ero1α inhibition stabilizes the RYR2-ERp44 complex, reducing proarrhythmic calcium waves and ventricular tachyarrhythmias in hypertrophic hearts.
biological.sample_size: Rat TAB model; isolated ventricular myocytes; HEK293 cells expressing human RYR2

biological.citation: Structural and Functional Regulation of RyR2 in Cardiac Calcium Handling and Arrhythmogenesis (PMID: 41898308)
biological.summary: RYR2 is the key sarcoplasmic reticulum calcium release channel mediating calcium-induced calcium release (CICR) in excitation-contraction coupling. RYR2 dysfunction causes store-overload-induced calcium release (SOICR) and arrhythmias. Key modulators (CaM, FKBP12.6, PKA/CaMKII) regulate RYR2 activity; ROS-induced RYR2 oxidation establishes a pathological calcium leak-ROS cycle in heart disease.

biological.citation: Ryanodine receptor 2 (RYR2) dysfunction activates the unfolded protein response and perturbs cardiomyocyte maturation (PMID: 35576474)
biological.summary: RYR2 depletion in cardiomyocytes triggers ER stress pathway activation through ATF4, impairing cardiomyocyte maturation. RYR2 regulates ER homeostasis essential for proper cardiomyocyte development. ER stress alleviator tauroursodeoxycholic acid partially rescues RYR2-depletion defects, and ATF4 overexpression recapitulates maturation defects.
biological.sample_size: Cas9/AAV9-mediated somatic mutagenesis in mice; genetic mosaic analysis

biological.citation: Foxp3-mediated blockage of ryanodine receptor 2 underlies contact-based suppression by regulatory T cells (PMID: 38099494)
biological.summary: Foxp3 transcription factor blocks RYR2 transcription in regulatory T cells, reducing basal calcium oscillations and m-calpain activities required for T cell disengagement from dendritic cells. RYR2 deficiency renders CD4+ T cells immune suppressive and phenotypically similar to Foxp3+ Tregs, revealing RYR2-mediated calcium signaling as a central effector mechanism of Treg immune suppression.
biological.sample_size: Viral infection, asthma, hypersensitivity, colitis, and tumor models in mice

biological.citation: Astrocyte-derived SerpinA3N promotes neuroinflammation and epileptic seizures by activating the NF-κB signaling pathway in mice with temporal lobe epilepsy (PMID: 37422673)
biological.summary: SerpinA3N interacts with RYR2 and promotes RYR2 phosphorylation in astrocytes during kainic acid-induced temporal lobe epilepsy. SerpinA3N-RYR2 interaction contributes to seizure-induced neuroinflammation through NF-κB pathway activation. This represents a novel mechanism linking RYR2 to seizure pathogenesis beyond cardiac function.
biological.sample_size: Kainic acid-induced temporal lobe epilepsy mouse model
